label: rem:upstream-mathlib-additions-detail
title: Details of the three Mathlib additions and their upstreaming targets
html:
Advances

(A) Real.dilog and Complex.dilog. The complexLiTwo definition implements a concrete tsum-based dilogarithm. The 1/k^2 factor guarantees summability on the closed unit disk. Mathlib provides Summable for geometric series. Appending absolute-convergence proofs makes this a candidate Mathlib PR.

(B) BlochWigner. The blochWigner definition utilizes Complex.log and Complex.arg from Mathlib. Proving the standard five-term pentagon identity for blochWigner closes gap (2). This proof reduces to the absolute convergence of complexLiTwo and the Spence-style functional equations for the real and imaginary parts of \mathrm{Li}_2.

(C) \mathrm{Cl}_2 functional equations. The reflection identity Cl_2(-θ) = -Cl_2(θ) is an unconditional Lean theorem. The proof applies Real.sin_neg and tsum_neg. This establishes the simplest \mathrm{Cl}_2 functional equation. Analogous tsum rearrangements extend this technique to periodicity identities such as Cl_2(θ + 2π) = Cl_2(θ).

Target translation

The conditional-class chain provides unconditional functional identities (Cl_2_neg, complexLiTwo_zero, blochWigner_zero) alongside concrete Lean definitions for complexLiTwo and blochWigner. This translates a prior axiomatic gap into specific, named Lean targets ready for upstreaming.
